As Lydia Deetz, a goth teenager in Tim Burton's "Beetlejuice" (1988), she won critical acclaim and widespread recognition.  After appearances in film and on television, Ryder continued her acting career with the cult film "Heathers" (1988), a controversial satire of teenage suicide and high school life that has since become a landmark teen film. Danny Elfman's theme for the film was arranged for the cartoon by Elfman himself.

The film employs both offbeat humor and serious philosophical musings.  It received critical acclaim and won numerous awards.

She first became known to a wider audience following her critically acclaimed work on the HBO television series "In Treatment" and she received a nomination for the Independent Spirit Award for Best Supporting Female for "That Evening Sun" (2009). The young man is taken in by a suburban family and falls in love with their teenage daughter Kim (Winona Ryder). One of the most successful and iconic actresses of the 1990s, she made her film debut in the film "Lucas" (1986).  As Lydia Deetz, a goth teenager in Tim Burton's "Beetlejuice" (1988), she won critical acclaim and widespread recognition.  After appearances in film and on television, Ryder continued her acting career with the cult film "Heathers" (1988), a controversial satire of teenage suicide and high school life that has since become a landmark teen film.
